title: afternoon-devx-scratchpad-todo
content:
Quick afternoon scratchpad (brain dump). Goal: capture small doc fixes, sample app gaps, and follow-ups so I don’t lose them into Slack threads. Mostly short action items + minimal repro notes.

Top priorities (short):
- [ ] docs: Quickstart Node example — streaming example broken for large responses (repro below).
- [ ] samples: add a small TS + Express sample showing function/tool calling + structured output. Keep it under 50 LOC.
- [ ] tutorial: guide for Dedicated vs Hosted decisions — add checklist for when customers should pick Dedicated (cost/throughput/security bullets).
- [ ] tests: add E2E snippet to CI that runs the node quickstart for smoke (10s timeout).

Notes / repros / context:
1) Streaming issue (Node quickstart):
- Steps: run examples/node/quickstart-stream.js with long_prompt.txt (approx 3k tokens). Node client returns an initial chunk then hangs until connection closed — looks like chunking vs event parsing.
- Hypothesis: client-side parser expects `data: [DONE]` but server sends one larger buffer followed by final object; streaming parser only triggers on line breaks.
- Quick workaround: add `\n\n` at end of each event in runtime -> but that’s not acceptable as default.
- Action: open a tiny PR in SDK to make streaming parser more tolerant (split on `\n` and also attempt JSON boundary parse). Link above (PR #482) is an initial attempt.

2) Sample app idea: "todo-list assistant" minimal sample that demonstrates: auth, streaming generation, function calling for CRUD, and a reranking step (embeddings + dot-product). Keep serverless-friendly. MVP: index.js + README + curl commands.

3) Tutorial flow gaps (obs from customer call):
- Customers ask: "How do I safely store user conversation logs?" Recommend sections: retention policy, PII redaction SDK snippet, KMS hint for Private deploys.
- Add small code snippet for redaction pipeline (pre-send regex/PII scrub + post-hash id).

4) Docs wording nit: hosted API page implies quantization is only for Private. Clarify: hosted supports quantized variants where available; Private supports custom quant settings.

5) UX note for Console Rollouts page: add example screenshot of canary config + fallback policy. Tiny screenshot missing in latest doc.

Open questions / things to ask during sync:
- Can we add a tiny internal flag to the runtime that forces event-by-event flushing for dev previews? (useful for streaming demos). -> ping infra/serving-runtime.
- Who owns the sample-app repo? Should live under `redwood-examples/` org. Ask Maya.

Small checklist for PRs I want to do today:
- [ ] Add tolerant streaming parser test (node). (target: small 1-file change).
- [ ] Create sample-app skeleton, add README and initial curl commands.
- [ ] Update quickstart README to include troubleshooting streaming section.

Snippet to paste into PR description (draft):
"Reconcile streaming consumer to accept chunked buffers without strict newline delimiters. Adds a fallback JSON boundary parser and unit tests covering both chunked and single-line payloads. Improves reliability for long-response demos and reduces flakiness in CI runs of examples."

Notes-to-self (random):
- Use Linear LR-2312 for tracking the sample app; include small checklist and assign to self.
- Add labels: docs, sdk, sample-app.
- Demo script for demo day: 1) create todo via function call, 2) append long item to trigger streaming, 3) show reranking call.

Meta: Keep this doc short-lived — move action items into Linear once I have a minimal repro for streaming. For now, leaving small todos here so I can grab them between meetings.

Last edited quick log:
- 2026-03-14 14:20: dumped streaming repro steps and PR link
- 2026-03-14 14:42 sketched sample-app flow + checklist

Unresolved (put a pin here):
- Confirm whether hosted models expose quantized variants for m-instruct family (ask model onboarding).
- Decide on sample-app license (MIT vs Apache) — default MIT?

If I get 30m: implement parser fix + smoke test and open PR.

End of scratchpad.
